claim: 11 subclones of the lab-adapted HB3 isolate of P. falciparum were obtained by serial dilution of the parent culture.
source: 11 subclones of the lab-adapted HB3 isolate of P. falciparum were obtained by serial dilution of the parent culture.
evidence: This is a direct statement about the experimental procedure performed by the authors.

claim: Transcript levels of 38 var genes were measured by quantitative PCR at 29–33 parasite generations after cloning and then at several time points over the following 60–79 generations.
source: The clones were cultivated and transcript levels of 38 var genes measured by quantitative PCR, first at 29–33 parasite generations (8–9 weeks) after cloning and then at several time points over the following 60–79 generations in each culture (Table 1)
evidence: This describes the experimental measurements performed in the study.

claim: The 38 genes measured comprised almost all known functional HB3 var genes and one partial gene.
source: These 38 genes comprised almost all known functional HB3 var genes (Kraemer et al., 2007; Rowe et al., 2009) and one partial gene.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work characterizing HB3 var genes.

claim: At the first observation, each of the 11 clones predominantly transcribed one of nine different var genes.
source: At the first observation, each of the 11 clones predominantly transcribed one of the nine different var genes, which were most likely the genes transcribed at the time of cloning.
evidence: This is a direct observation from the experimental data.

claim: The nine starter genes were representative of the var repertoire diversity in terms of chromosomal location and Ups type.
source: Importantly, these nine genes—hereafter referred to as 'starter genes'—were representative of the var repertoire diversity in terms of chromosomal location and Ups type.
evidence: This is an assessment of the starter genes based on their characteristics.

claim: The centrally located, UpsC starter gene var29 in culture #8 accounted for more than 90% of the total transcript level at the first measurement and remained the dominant variant over the following 60 generations.
source: For example, the centrally located, UpsC starter gene var29 in culture #8 accounted for more than 90% of the total transcript level at the first measurement and remained the dominant variant over the following 60 generations.
evidence: This is a specific observation from the experimental data for culture #8.

claim: The transcript level of the var35 starter gene of culture #11 (subtelomeric, UpsA promoter type) was already below 50% of the total transcript level at the first observation and continued to decline during the time course of culture.
source: In contrast, the transcript level of the var35 starter gene of culture #11 (subtelomeric, UpsA promoter type) was already below 50% of the total transcript level at the point of the first observation (approximately 30 generations post cloning) and continued to decline during the time course of culture, to be eventually replaced by other genes as dominant transcripts.
evidence: This is a specific observation from the experimental data for culture #11.

claim: Most cultures converged towards high transcription of var27 and/or var29.
source: Of particular interest was the apparent convergence of most cultures towards high transcription of var27 and/or var29 (Figure 1, Figure 1—figure supplements 1 and 2)
evidence: This observation is supported by both the text and the figures showing transcript levels over time.

claim: var27 and var29 are both situated in central chromosomal location but have different promoter types (UpsB and UpsC, respectively).
source: which are both situated in central chromosomal location but have different promoter types (UpsB and UpsC, respectively).
evidence: This is a characterization of the genetic features of these two genes.

claim: The convergence of cultures towards var27 and var29 indicates that antigenic switching in P. falciparum might be governed by an activation hierarchy.
source: In light of the very different initial conditions, in terms of var gene transcription levels at which these cultures were established, this indicates that antigenic switching in P. falciparum might be governed by an activation hierarchy.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the observed convergence pattern.

claim: Var gene switching can be fully described dynamically by two sets of parameters: off-rates and switch biases.
source: We have previously proposed that var gene switching can be fully described dynamically by two sets of parameters ('Materials and methods' and [Recker et al., 2011]).
evidence: This is based on a previously published model by the authors.

claim: Both the 16-gene and 38-gene models gave good fits between the data and predicted transcript levels.
source: We applied our algorithm to the full 38-gene data set and separately to a reduced set of the 16 most transcribed genes, and both models generally gave good and similar fits between the data and predicted transcript levels (Figure 1—figure supplements 1 and 2)
evidence: This is a statement about the model fitting results.

claim: Parameter estimates of the starter genes were more accurate and resulted in much narrower credible intervals due to higher signal to noise ratios.
source: Due to higher signal to noise ratios, parameter estimates of the starter genes (indicated in red) were more accurate and resulted in much narrower credible intervals, as indicated by less fuzzy rings that represent respective switch probabilities.
evidence: This is an assessment of the reliability of parameter estimates based on data quality.

claim: Estimated off-rates ranged from 0.3% to more than 5% per generation, with a mean of approximately 2.9%.
source: Estimated off-rates ranged from 0.3% to more than 5% per generation, with a mean of approximately 2.9% (Table 2).
evidence: This is a summary of the estimated parameter values from the model.

claim: var29 and var27 had exceptionally low off-rates of approximately 0.3% and 0.8%, respectively.
source: Notably, the two most transcribed genes, var29 and var27 (both centrally located on chromosome 4), had exceptionally low off-rates of approximately 0.3% and 0.8%, respectively
evidence: This is a specific finding from the parameter estimation.

claim: The other starter genes switched off at rates between 1.4% and 3.5% per generation.
source: whereas the other starter genes switched off at rates between 1.4% and 3.5% per generation.
evidence: This is a summary of estimated off-rates for other starter genes.

claim: Off-rates of centrally located genes are significantly lower than of genes in subtelomeric regions (Welch's t = 3.3, p=0.002).
source: In general we found off-rates of centrally located genes to be significantly lower than of genes in subtelomeric regions (Welch's t = 3.3, p=0.002), as shown in Figure 3.
evidence: This is a statistical finding from comparing off-rates between gene groups.

claim: The difference in off-rates between central and subtelomeric genes remained significant (p=0.035) when accounting for uncertainty in estimates.
source: This result remained significant (p=0.035) when we accounted for uncertainty in our estimates ('Materials and methods').
evidence: This is a statistical result after applying a more rigorous analysis.

claim: There was no significant difference in off-rates between subtelomeric UpsA genes and other subtelomeric genes (Welch's t = 0.65, p=0.54).
source: We compared the off-rates of the subtelomeric UpsA genes with those of other subtelomeric genes and found no significant difference (Welch's t = 0.65, p=0.54; accounting for uncertainty p=0.55), as shown in Figure 3.
evidence: This is a statistical finding from comparing off-rates between UpsA and non-UpsA subtelomeric genes.

claim: Among centrally located genes, there was no significant difference in off-rates between UpsB and UpsC genes (Welch's t = 0.44, p=0.44).
source: Among centrally located genes we compared UpsB with UpsC and again found no significant difference (Figure 3; Welch's t = 0.44, p=0.44; accounting for uncertainty p=0.57).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from comparing off-rates between UpsB and UpsC central genes.

claim: The rate at which transcriptionally active var genes become silenced is less dependent on promoter type than on chromosomal location.
source: This lends support to a previous study suggesting that the rate at which transcriptionally active var genes become silenced is less dependent on promoter type than on chromosomal location (Frank et al., 2007).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the statistical analyses and supported by a previous study.

claim: Only a minority of genes were ever highly transcribed during the experiment.
source: In each of our cultures, gene transcription levels spanned several orders of magnitude, and only a minority of genes were ever highly transcribed during the experiment.
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental data.

claim: The ranking of gene activation was highly correlated between cultures (Spearman's ρ > 0.8, p=10−5 for all pairs).
source: Pair-wise comparison showed that the ranking was highly correlated between the cultures (Spearman's ρ > 0.8, p=10−5 for all pairs)
evidence: This is a statistical finding from comparing gene rankings across cultures.

claim: The outcome of antigenic switching in P. falciparum is largely governed by an activation hierarchy that is independent of the currently activated gene.
source: suggesting that the outcome of antigenic switching in P. falciparum, or at least within the HB3 isolate, is largely governed by an activation hierarchy that is independent of the currently activated gene.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the correlation analysis of gene rankings.

claim: All genes were found to have high switch biases towards the same few genes.
source: All genes were found to have high switch biases towards the same few genes, which explain the observed convergence in var transcription in our cultures.
evidence: This is a finding from the switch bias parameter estimates.

claim: The highest biases across the repertoire were found towards var29 and var27.
source: As expected, the highest biases across the repertoire were found towards var29 and var27, with some genes also frequently switching towards var35 and/or var28 (both UpsC-types in central chromosomal location).
evidence: This is a specific finding from the switch bias estimates.

claim: There was a clear hierarchy in gene activation biases spanning over three orders of magnitude.
source: As shown in Table 2, there was a clear hierarchy in gene activation biases spanning over three orders of magnitude.
evidence: This is an observation from the estimated activation bias parameters.

claim: Activation biases of centrally located var genes are significantly higher than those of subtelomeric genes (Welch's t = 2.8, p=0.009).
source: Analysing for possible associations with genetic attributes confirmed that activation biases of centrally located var genes are significantly higher than those of subtelomeric genes (Figure 4, Welch's t = 2.8, p=0.009; accounting for uncertainty p=0.011).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from comparing activation biases between gene groups.

claim: Of the highest four activation biases, three belonged to neighbouring genes on chromosome 4: var29, var27 and var28.
source: In fact, of the highest four activation biases, three belonged to neighbouring genes on chromosome 4: var29, var27 and var28.
evidence: This is a specific observation from the activation bias estimates.

claim: No significant and independent effect of promoter type on activation bias was found.
source: Importantly, no significant and independent effect of promoter type was found, which again points towards a strong influence of chromosomal location on var gene activation.
evidence: This is a conclusion from statistical analyses of activation biases.

claim: Activation biases differed significantly depending on gene length (F = 9.7, p=0.004) as well as chromosomal location (F = 8.1, p=0.007) and the interaction of these two factors (F = 5.0, p=0.032).
source: Grouping genes depending on whether they encoded only four domains (short genes) or more than four domains (long genes) showed that activation biases differed significantly depending on gene length (Figure 4, F = 9.7, p=0.004) as well as chromosomal location (F = 8.1, p=0.007) and the interaction of these two factors (F = 5.0, p=0.032).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from ANOVA analysis of activation biases.

claim: Central var genes encoding only four binding domains had on average a 10 times higher activation bias than the rest of the repertoire.
source: As such, central var genes encoding only four binding domains (also known as Type 1 var genes [Gardner et al., 2002]) had on average a 10 times higher activation bias than the rest of the repertoire.
evidence: This is a specific finding from the analysis of activation biases by gene characteristics.

claim: The model with individual switch biases was significantly more likely than the model where all sets of switch biases were identical (F = 1.84, p<0.0001).
source: A likelihood ratio test indicated that the model with individual switch biases was significantly more likely than the second model (F = 1.84, p<0.0001), confirming that antigenic switching in P. falciparum is not only controlled by an activation hierarchy but also influenced by the currently active gene.
evidence: This is a statistical finding from model comparison.

claim: Antigenic switching in P. falciparum is not only controlled by an activation hierarchy but also influenced by the currently active gene.
source: confirming that antigenic switching in P. falciparum is not only controlled by an activation hierarchy but also influenced by the currently active gene.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the model comparison results.

claim: Switch biases were higher between var genes with matching chromosomal locations than between differently located genes (Welch's t = 2.2, p=0.029).
source: We again tested for associations with chromosomal location and promoter type ('Materials and methods'), which indicated that switch biases were higher between var genes with matching chromosomal locations than between differently located genes (Figure 5; Welch's t = 2.2, p=0.029)
evidence: This is a statistical finding from analyzing switch bias patterns.

claim: No significant association was found between switch biases and matching Ups types or gene lengths.
source: whereas no significant association was found between switch biases and matching Ups types or gene lengths.
evidence: This is a statistical finding from analyzing switch bias patterns.

claim: Statistical significance of the association between switch biases and matching chromosomal locations was lost when accounting for uncertainty in parameter estimates.
source: This result needs to be confirmed with larger data sets, however, as statistical significance was lost when we accounted for uncertainty in our parameter estimates.
evidence: This is a statement about the robustness of the statistical finding.

claim: The degree by which var genes share sequence blocks is positively correlated with activation bias, independently of chromosomal location and gene length (F = 8.8, p=0.006).
source: The inclusion of network centrality as an explanatory variable in the previous ANOVA model confirmed that the degree by which var genes share sequence blocks is positively correlated with activation bias, independently of chromosomal location and gene length (Figure 6A; F = 8.8, p=0.006 for the model comparison; accounting for uncertainty p=0.006).
evidence: This is a statistical finding from analyzing the relationship between sequence similarity and activation bias.

claim: Simulation of gene conversion, in which pairs of genes were chosen at random weighted by their activation bias, showed a strong positive correlation between activation bias and relatedness in terms of network centrality.
source: To test this we explicitly simulated gene conversion, in which pairs of genes were chosen at random, weighted by their activation bias and homology blocks copied between them ('Materials and methods). As expected, we found a strong positive correlation between activation bias and our measure of relatedness in terms of network centrality (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a finding from a simulation study testing a hypothesis.

claim: Average sequence conservation of all domains is significantly and positively correlated with activation bias, independently of chromosomal location and gene length (F = 13.6, p=0.0009).
source: Indeed, using the average sequence conservation of all domains as a measure of population level diversity (Buckee and Recker, 2012), we again found this to be significantly and positively correlated, independently of chromosomal location and gene length (Figure 6C; F = 13.6, p=0.0009 for the model comparison; accounting for uncertainty p=0.0006)
evidence: This is a statistical finding from analyzing the relationship between sequence conservation and activation bias.

claim: Active gene transcription plays a role in generating antigenic diversity in P. falciparum malaria.
source: suggesting a role of active gene transcription in generating antigenic diversity in P. falciparum malaria.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the correlation between activation bias and sequence diversity.

claim: Var genes located near the centres of chromosomes tend to be more highly transcribed in vitro than those in subtelomeric location.
source: Several studies have noted that var genes located near the centres of chromosomes tend to be more highly transcribed in vitro than those in subtelomeric location (Frank et al., 2007; Peters et al., 2007; Enderes et al., 2011; Zhang et al., 2011; Fastman et al., 2012)
evidence: This is a statement about findings from multiple previous studies.

claim: High transcription levels are confined to a subset of central genes that encode only four PfEMP1 binding domains (Type 1 var genes).
source: In this study, we found that high transcription levels are confined to a subset of central genes that encode only four PfEMP1 binding domains (termed Type 1 var genes [Gardner et al., 2002])
evidence: This is a finding from the current study.

claim: High transcription levels are the result of high activation biases rather than low off-rates.
source: and, importantly, are the result of high activation biases rather than low off-rates.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the parameter estimation and analysis.

claim: Off-rates, at least within a biologically plausible range, can have only a modest effect on the total transcript levels within parasite populations.
source: This is consistent with our previous study using artificial transcription data, which also showed that off-rates, at least within a biologically plausible range, can have only a modest effect on the total transcript levels within parasite populations (Noble and Recker, 2012).
evidence: This is a statement about findings from a previous study by the authors.

claim: In NF54, centrally located var genes encoding only four binding domains were more highly transcribed than the rest of the repertoire (Welch's t = 2.3, p=0.02).
source: Reanalysis of data from a recent study on the NF54 parasite strain by Fastman et al. (2012) supports these findings. Consistent with our results for HB3, centrally located var genes encoding only four binding domains were more highly transcribed than the rest of the repertoire (Welch's t = 2.3, p=0.02)
evidence: This is a finding from reanalysis of published data from another strain.

claim: In NF54, PF3D7_0809100, PF3D7_0421300 and PF3D7_0800100 were the most highly transcribed genes.
source: with PF3D7_0809100, PF3D7_0421300 and PF3D7_0800100 being the most highly transcribed genes.
evidence: This is a finding from reanalysis of published NF54 data.

claim: PF3D7_0809100 has previously been reported as the most transcribed var gene in NF54 bulk culture.
source: According to our model, these are predicted to have high activation bias, and indeed, PF3D7_0809100 has previously been reported as the most transcribed var gene in NF54 bulk culture
evidence: This is a statement about a previous finding in the literature.

claim: PF3D7_0421300 and PF3D7_0800100 were found to be the two genes most commonly activated by var gene switching in previous studies.
source: whereas PF3D7_0421300 and PF3D7_0800100 were found to be the two genes most commonly activated by var gene switching in previous studies (Dzikowski et al., 2006; Frank et al., 2007; Enderes et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a statement about previous findings in the literature.

claim: In NF54, gene transcription levels were positively correlated with relatedness to the rest of the repertoire in terms of shared DBL1 and CIDR1 homology blocks (Spearman's ρ = 0.3, p=0.044).
source: Also in agreement with our results, NF54 gene transcription levels were positively correlated with relatedness to the rest of the repertoire in terms of shared DBL1 and CIDR1 homology blocks (Spearman's ρ = 0.3, p=0.044).
evidence: This is a finding from reanalysis of published NF54 data.

claim: The direction of transcriptional switching between var genes depends not only on intrinsic activation biases but also on the particular preferences of each deactivating gene.
source: Our results further indicate that the direction of transcriptional switching between var genes depends not only on intrinsic activation biases but also on the particular preferences of each deactivating gene.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the analysis of switch biases.

claim: Variations in switch biases are expected to play a much greater role during infection, where factors such as immune responses and binding affinities can significantly alter the var gene expression profiles.
source: Even though these variations were found to have only a modest effect on in vitro switching, they are expected to play a much greater role during infection, where factors such as immune responses and binding affinities can significantly alter the var gene expression profiles.
evidence: This is a speculation about the in vivo relevance of the findings.

claim: The combination of an activation hierarchy and specific variations in switch biases could explain the previously proposed source-sink model underlying antigenic switching in P. falciparum.
source: Furthermore, the combination of an activation hierarchy and these specific variations could explain our previously proposed source-sink model underlying antigenic switching in P. falciparum (Recker et al., 2011), in which genes with high in-degrees, i.e., those most commonly switched to, correspond to the genes here identified as having high activation biases.
evidence: This is a connection drawn between current findings and a previous model.

claim: The discovery of intrinsic var gene activation biases and their associations with chromosomal locations and other genetic features could have important implications for future studies.
source: The discovery of intrinsic var gene activation biases and their associations with chromosomal locations and other genetic features could therefore have important implications for future studies.
evidence: This is a statement about the potential impact of the findings.

claim: Gene length is positively correlated with sequence conservation.
source: For example, in a recent study it was found that gene length is positively correlated with sequence conservation (Buckee and Recker, 2012)
evidence: This is a statement about a finding from a previous study.

claim: Long var genes are more often positioned in subtelomeric regions.
source: and long var genes are more often positioned in subtelomeric regions.
evidence: This is a statement about a known characteristic of var genes.

claim: The correlation between activation bias and relatedness suggests a role of gene transcription in facilitating recombination and therefore in generating and maintaining antigenic diversity in P. falciparum.
source: Nevertheless, the correlation between activation bias and relatedness, which was found to be independent of chromosomal location, gene length and upstream promoter, suggests a role of gene transcription in facilitating recombination and therefore in generating and maintaining antigenic diversity in P. falciparum.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the correlation analysis.

claim: Transcription-associated recombination has been observed in other eukaryotes.
source: Transcription-associated recombination has been observed in other eukaryotes and may result from increased accessibility to recombination proteins or from stalled replication forks (Prado and Aguilera, 2005; Gottipati and Helleday, 2009).
evidence: This is a statement about a phenomenon observed in other organisms.

claim: For P. falciparum, transcription-associated recombination could help to explain why different groups of var genes within the repertoire display very different levels of diversity within the population.
source: Importantly, for P. falciparum this phenomenon could help to explain why different groups of var genes within the repertoire display very different levels of diversity within the population (Buckee et al., 2009; Buckee and Recker, 2012).
evidence: This is a hypothesis connecting transcription-associated recombination to observed diversity patterns.

claim: Some var genes may be under balancing selection, whereby the relative sequence conservation of longer genes could be due to optimised functionality.
source: It is further possible that some var genes are under balancing selection, whereby the relative sequence conservation of longer genes could be due to optimised functionality, for example in terms of binding avidity and/or affinity.
evidence: This is a speculation about evolutionary pressures on var genes.

claim: Various in vivo studies have reported UpsA var genes to be over-expressed during infections in individuals with little previous exposure.
source: That is, various in vivo studies have reported UpsA var genes to be over-expressed during infections in individuals with little previous exposure (Jensen et al., 2004; Bull et al., 2005; Lavstsen et al., 2005; Kyriacou et al., 2006; Warimwe et al., 2009), despite their low activation rates in vitro.
evidence: This is a statement about findings from multiple in vivo studies.

claim: Each var repertoire consists of a set of relatively long and conserved genes, such as those predominantly found within the UpsA group, and another, short and diverse set of genes, such as those predominantly found within the UpsB and UpsC groups.
source: Each var repertoire consists of a set of relatively long and conserved genes, such as those predominantly found with in the UpsA group, and another, short and diverse set of genes, such as those predominantly found within the UpsB and UpsC groups (Buckee and Recker, 2012).
evidence: This is a statement about var gene repertoire structure from a previous study.

claim: Under the assumption that more conserved genes have an in vivo survival advantage, these variants will dominate early infections in naive hosts, regardless of activation rates.
source: Under the assumption that more conserved genes have an in vivo survival advantage, possibly due to higher binding affinities (Avril et al., 2012; Claessens et al., 2012; Lavstsen et al., 2012), these variants will dominate early infections in naive hosts, regardless of activation rates.
evidence: This is a hypothesis about in vivo selection based on gene characteristics.

claim: The lower sequence diversity of conserved genes will lead to a more rapid acquisition of protective immunity, causing a transition towards the expression of more diverse variants.
source: Their lower sequence diversity, however, will then lead to a more rapid acquisition of protective immunity, causing a transition towards the expression of more diverse variants, facilitated by their inherent activation biases.
evidence: This is a hypothesis about the dynamics of immunity acquisition and variant expression.

claim: The proposed order in which individuals acquire immunity (anti-UpsA followed by anti-UpsB/C) is less determined by the Ups group itself and is more a consequence of within-host selection of long, conserved genes.
source: In light of this we would also speculate that the proposed order in which individuals acquire immunity (anti-UpsA followed by anti-UpsB/C), as well as the proposed associations between the expression of UpsA var genes and severe disease outcome, especially in young children, is less determined by the Ups group itself and is more a consequence of within-host selection of long, conserved genes, which are often but not exclusively found within the UpsA group.
evidence: This is a speculation about the mechanisms underlying immunity acquisition patterns.

claim: Selection pressures operating on multiple ecological scales have shaped the phenotypic plasticity embodied within the antigenic repertoire of P. falciparum.
source: Together, these results demonstrate how selection pressures operating on multiple ecological scales have shaped the phenotypic plasticity embodied within the antigenic repertoire of P. falciparum.
evidence: This is a broad conclusion about the evolutionary forces shaping var gene diversity.

claim: Var genes and the molecular mechanisms that underlie their sequential activation and silencing have co-evolved to allow the parasite to express the most advantageous phenotype in response to its current environment.
source: Within this setup, var genes and the molecular mechanisms that underlie their sequential activation and silencing have co-evolved to allow the parasite to express the most advantageous phenotype in response to its current environment.
evidence: This is a conclusion about the adaptive significance of the var gene switching system.

claim: Acquired antibody-mediated immunity against Plasmodium falciparum is directed against the disease-causing, intra-erythrocytic life-stage of the parasite's life-cycle.
source: Acquired antibody-mediated immunity against Plasmodium falciparum is directed against the disease-causing, intra-erythrocytic life-stage of the parasite's life-cycle.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about malaria immunity.

claim: Continual exposure to P. falciparum infection can lead to a form of semi-immunity, whereby protection against life-threatening disease is acquired after a few infections only.
source: Continual exposure to P. falciparum infection can lead to a form of semi-immunity, whereby protection against life-threatening disease is acquired after a few infections only (Gupta et al., 1999)
evidence: This is a statement about malaria immunity supported by a citation.

claim: Sterile and long-lasting immunity against infection is never achieved through natural exposure to P. falciparum.
source: whereas sterile and long-lasting immunity against infection is never achieved through natural exposure (Greenwood et al., 1987; Marsh, 1992; Tran et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a statement about malaria immunity supported by citations.

claim: The process of natural acquired immunity coincides with a transition from acute and severe infection in young children to asymptomatic carriage in older individuals.
source: The process of natural acquired immunity therefore coincides with a transition from acute and severe infection in young children to asymptomatic carriage in older individuals (Marsh and Snow, 1997).
evidence: This is a statement about the age-dependent pattern of malaria immunity supported by a citation.

claim: P. falciparum erythrocyte membrane protein 1 (PfEMP1) is the major parasite virulence factor and variant antigen.
source: At the core of this variable outcome of infection and poor development of immunity lies the major parasite virulence factor and variant antigen, P. falciparum erythrocyte membrane protein 1 (PfEMP1).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about PfEMP1.

claim: Members of the PfEMP1 family are expressed on the surface of infected red blood cells and are involved in the binding of parasitised cells to other host cells and tissues.
source: Members of this family of proteins are expressed on the surface of infected red blood cells and are involved in the binding of parasitised cells to other host cells and tissues (for an overview see Kraemer and Smith, (2006)).
evidence: This is a statement about PfEMP1 function supported by a citation.

claim: The binding phenotypes conferred by PfEMP1 are believed to enhance parasite survival by avoiding splenic clearance.
source: The conferred binding phenotypes are believed to enhance parasite survival by avoiding splenic clearance (Boone and Watters, 1995; Buffet et al., 2009)
evidence: This is a statement about PfEMP1 function supported by citations.

claim: PfEMP1 binding phenotypes contribute to malaria pathology through parasite sequestration in the deep vasculature.
source: and also contribute to malaria pathology through parasite sequestration in the deep vasculature (Ockenhouse et al., 1991; Pongponratn et al., 1991).
evidence: This is a statement about PfEMP1's role in pathology supported by citations.

claim: Mutually exclusive transcriptional switching between PfEMP1 variants during the course of an infection affords the parasite an immune evasion strategy and a means to exploit different host tissues.
source: Mutually exclusive transcriptional switching between PfEMP1 variants during the course of an infection thus affords the parasite an immune evasion strategy and a means to exploit different host tissues (Roberts et al., 1992; Smith et al., 1995).
evidence: This is a statement about the function of var gene switching supported by citations.

claim: Each haploid parasite genome contains approximately 60 members of the var gene family encoding distinct PfEMP1 variants.
source: Each haploid parasite genome contains approximately 60 members of the var gene family (Gardner et al., 2002) encoding distinct PfEMP1 variants
evidence: This is a statement about var gene repertoire size supported by a citation.

claim: There is a high degree of divergence between the antigenic repertoires of any two parasites.
source: with a high degree of divergence between the antigenic repertoires of any two parasites.
evidence: This is a statement about var gene diversity.

claim: The high diversity of var genes and var gene repertoires is predominantly generated and maintained by frequent recombination and gene conversion events.
source: The high diversity of var genes and var gene repertoires is predominantly generated and maintained by frequent recombination and gene conversion events (Deitsch et al., 1999; Ward et al., 1999; Freitas-Junior et al., 2000; Taylor et al., 2000; Kraemer et al., 2007; Frank et al., 2008)
evidence: This is a statement about the mechanisms generating var gene diversity supported by citations.

claim: Recombination and gene conversion have resulted in a high degree of mosaicism within var genes.
source: which has also resulted in a high degree of mosaicism within these genes (Ward et al., 1999; Taylor et al., 2000; Bull et al., 2008).
evidence: This is a statement about var gene structure supported by citations.

claim: The modular and highly polymorphic, extracellular portion of PfEMP1 is composed of a variable number of Duffy-binding-like domains (DBL; at least two and up to seven per gene) and cysteine-rich interdomain regions (CIDR; up to two per gene).
source: The modular and highly polymorphic, extracellular portion of PfEMP1 is composed of a variable number of Duffy-binding-like domains (DBL; at least two and up to seven per gene) and cysteine-rich interdomain regions (CIDR; up to two per gene) (Kraemer et al., 2007).
evidence: This is a statement about PfEMP1 structure supported by a citation.

claim: Distinct associations with severe malaria have been identified for several var genes.
source: Despite the overall diversity of var genes at the sequence level, distinct associations with severe malaria have been identified for several such genes (Salanti et al., 2003; Jensen et al., 2004)
evidence: This is a statement about var gene associations with disease supported by citations.

claim: The involvement of var2csa in pregnancy-associated malaria is the clearest example of a var gene association with severe disease.
source: with the involvement of var2csa in pregnancy-associated malaria being the clearest example to date (Salanti et al., 2004)
evidence: This is a statement about a specific var gene association supported by a citation.

claim: Associations with severe malaria have been identified for particular DBL domains and combinations of DBL and CIDR.
source: as well as associations with particular DBL domains (Warimwe et al., 2009) and combinations of DBL and CIDR (Avril et al., 2012; Claessens et al., 2012; Lavstsen et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a statement about domain-level associations with disease supported by citations.

claim: Var genes can be classified according to a conserved upstream promoter sequence into four types termed UpsA, UpsB, UpsC, and UpsE.
source: Var genes can also be classified according to a conserved upstream promoter sequence into four types termed UpsA, UpsB, UpsC, and UpsE (Lavstsen et al., 2003).
